plan.contextChunk: This figure is a perspective sketch of the magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire, combined with a right-hand-rule demonstration. A gray cylindrical wire runs horizontally across the full width of the drawing. At the left, a realistically rendered right hand grips the wire in a closed fist with the thumb extended along it toward the right; just beyond the hand, a short red arrow labeled I points the same way. Along the right half of the wire, four identical sets of concentric blue circles encircle it, each set drawn as nested ellipses so they read as circles centered on the wire in planes perpendicular to it. Within every set the rings crowd together near the wire and stand progressively farther apart outward, and each carries arrowheads marking a common sense of circulation that matches the wrap of the fingers. A bold label B with a vector arrow sits above the rightmost set. Pairing the gripping hand with the ring sets asks the reader to match thumb to current and finger wrap to field direction, while the widening spacing encodes the field weakening with distance.

four identical sets of concentric blue field circles encircling the wire along its right half, each set lying in a plane perpendicular to the wire (drawn as nested ellipses in this view)

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Wire: cylinder along +X (screen-right), length 22 units, radius 0.16, centered at origin, spanning x = -11 to +11; color mid-gray #9aa0a6 with a lighter #d8dce0 highlight along its top. Hand: positioned at x = -6, fist closed around the wire (fist ~2.6 units tall, 2.2 deep), skin fill #f2d0a9 with #c88f5e outlines; thumb extended horizontally along +X, thumb tip reaching x ≈ -4.4, resting just below the wire; fingers curl over the top of the wire and down the far side (curl sense matches field for I to the right). Red current arrow: straight shaft on the wire axis from x = -3.2 to x = -2.0 at y = 0 (drawn just below/on the wire), color #b02a2a, arrowhead length 0.35; italic label 'I' at (-2.9, -0.75). Four ring sets centered on the wire axis at x = 0.5, 4.0, 7.5, 11.0 minus frame offset — use x = 1, 4, 7, 10 — each set in the Y-Z plane (perpendicular to wire). Per set, four concentric rings of radius 0.5, 0.95, 1.6, 2.5 world units (spacing 0.45, 0.65, 0.9 — crowding near the wire, widening outward), tube/line width ~0.035, color #1f7ac0. Each ring carries 1-2 arrowheads at roughly the bottom-front of the circle showing circulation: for I to the right (+X), circulation is counterclockwise when viewed from +X looking back toward -X (right-hand rule), which in this three-quarter view reads as arrows coming down the near side. Label 'B' with overbar vector arrow, bold black, placed above the rightmost ring set at (10, 3.2, 0). Radial marker: short line from wire axis at x = 7 outward in +Y (and slightly toward viewer) to radius r, with a highlighted amber #e8a33d ring of that radius drawn in the same plane; readout text near the marker. Physics: B = mu0*I/(2*pi*r) with I = 10 A, so B(microtesla) = 2.0/r(cm); at r = 1.5 cm B = 1.33 microtesla, at r = 6 cm B = 0.33 microtesla. Slider r in cm maps to world radius via world_r = 0.42 * r_cm so that r = 1.2 cm sits on the innermost ring and r = 6 cm on the outermost. Background white.
interactionPlan.notes: Build rings as THREE.TorusGeometry (thin tube) or Line loops in the Y-Z plane, grouped per set so the whole group can be rotated 180 degrees about Y, or arrowheads swapped, when current reverses. Arrowheads: small ConeGeometry oriented tangent to the ring; store tangent sign in a uniform/state so the toggle just negates it (animate the flip over ~400 ms so the reversal is visibly continuous). Hand can be a low-poly stylized mesh or a flat billboarded sprite/SVG texture facing the camera; if billboarded, mirror it horizontally on current reversal and re-point the thumb. Wire uses MeshStandardMaterial with low roughness plus a thin emissive highlight strip; render the wire after/through ring groups with correct depth so near rings occlude the wire and far rings are occluded (no depthWrite tricks needed if geometry is real 3D). Keep OrbitControls limited to azimuth -60..60 deg and elevation -20..45 deg so the figure never flips. Labels (I, B, readout) as CSS2DObject/HTML overlays anchored to world positions so they stay crisp and upright while orbiting.

authoredContext:
The magnetic field lines of the infinite wire are circular and centered at the wire (the figure), and they are identical in every plane perpendicular to the wire. Since the field decreases with distance from the wire, the spacing of the field lines must increase correspondingly with distance. The direction of this magnetic field may be found with a second form of the right-hand rule (illustrated in the figure). If you hold the wire with your right hand so that your thumb points along the current, then your fingers wrap around the wire in the same sense as B→.

Some magnetic field lines of an infinite wire. The direction of B→ can be found with a form of the right-hand rule.

This figure demonstrates the right-hand rule. The wire is held with the right hand so that the thumb points along the current. The fingers wrap around the wire in the same sense as the magnetic field.

The direction of the field lines can be observed experimentally by placing several small compass needles on a circle near the wire, as illustrated in the figure. When there is no current in the wire, the needles align with Earth’s magnetic field. However, when a large current is sent through the wire, the compass needles all point tangent to the circle. Iron filings sprinkled on a horizontal surface also delineate the field lines, as shown in the figure.

attempts.html:
Magnetic field of a straight wire
B = 1.33 µT
B = μ0I / (2πr), I = 10 A → B(µT) = 2.0 / r(cm)
Guided tour
Drag the figure to orbit: the nested “ellipses” are true circles in planes perpendicular to the wire. Click the wire or a ring for an explanation.
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The right fist is drastically undersized and crudely formed — in the source it is a large, prominent hand gripping the wire with four clearly curled fingers and a long extended thumb; in the render it is a small tan blob whose fingers/thumb are essentially unreadable at the default framing.

The default camera is rotated well off the source's wire-perpendicular view, so the field loops render as narrow vertical ellipses and the rightmost ring set collapses almost to a straight line, whereas the source shows four clearly circular/near-circular nested ring sets.
Quantitative readout is physically wrong by a factor of 100: μ0I/(2πr) with I = 10 A gives B(µT) = 200/r(cm), not 2.0/r(cm); the panel shows 1.33 µT at r = 1.5 cm instead of ~133 µT.
The 'I' and 'B⃗' labels are rendered very small and faint relative to the source, where 'B⃗' is a large bold header above the rings and 'I' is clearly readable beside the red arrow.
Extra amber highlight ring + radial spoke + floating r/B text box at x = 7 have no counterpart in the source figure.
The wire runs diagonally across the frame rather than as the clean horizontal rod of the source, and the whole assembly occupies only the left-middle of the canvas.
evaluation.notes: All the source elements (wire, gripping hand, red current arrow, four nested blue ring sets with tangential arrowheads, B label) are present with correct right-hand-rule circulation and a rich set of working interactions, but the hand is far too small and crude, the camera compresses the rings into narrow ellipses (rightmost set nearly edge-on), labels are faint, and the B magnitude formula/readout is off by a factor of 100.

feedback.rationale: All conceptually correct elements are present with proper right-hand-rule structure; the issues are implementation-level — default camera angle, hand scale/detail, label sizing, extraneous overlay elements, and a unit-conversion bug in the B readout.

evaluation.notes: Composition, ring sets, colors and the physics (right-hand circulation sense, 1/r falloff) are correct and the interaction set is rich and well-tied to the concept, but the fist geometry reads as a stack of rings rather than a hand, the B-vector label shows a broken glyph, and the oblique camera tilts the wire away from the source's horizontal layout.

feedback.rationale: The concept, decomposition, and interaction design are correct (concept 5, interactivity 5); the issues are execution-level — hand geometry primitives, a broken label glyph, camera/wire orientation, and arrow sizing — all fixable in the rendering.

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a perspective sketch of the magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire, combined with a right-hand-rule demonstration. A gray cylindrical wire runs horizontally across the full width of the drawing. At the left, a realistically rendered right hand grips the wire in a closed fist with the thumb extended along it toward the right; just beyond the hand, a short red arrow labeled I points the same way. Along the right half of the wire, four identical sets of concentric blue circles encircle it, each set drawn as nested ellipses so they read as circles centered on the wire in planes perpendicular to it. Within every set the rings crowd together near the wire and stand progressively farther apart outward, and each carries arrowheads marking a common sense of circulation that matches the wrap of the fingers. A bold label B with a vector arrow sits above the rightmost set. Pairing the gripping hand with the ring sets asks the reader to match thumb to current and finger wrap to field direction, while the widening spacing encodes the field weakening with distance.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Wire: cylinder along +X (screen-right), length 22 units, radius 0.16, centered at origin, spanning x = -11 to +11; color mid-gray #9aa0a6 with a lighter #d8dce0 highlight along its top. Hand: positioned at x = -6, fist closed around the wire (fist ~2.6 units tall, 2.2 deep), skin fill #f2d0a9 with #c88f5e outlines; thumb extended horizontally along +X, thumb tip reaching x ≈ -4.4, resting just below the wire; fingers curl over the top of the wire and down the far side (curl sense matches field for I to the right). Red current arrow: straight shaft on the wire axis from x = -3.2 to x = -2.0 at y = 0 (drawn just below/on the wire), color #b02a2a, arrowhead length 0.35; italic label 'I' at (-2.9, -0.75). Four ring sets centered on the wire axis at x = 0.5, 4.0, 7.5, 11.0 minus frame offset — use x = 1, 4, 7, 10 — each set in the Y-Z plane (perpendicular to wire). Per set, four concentric rings of radius 0.5, 0.95, 1.6, 2.5 world units (spacing 0.45, 0.65, 0.9 — crowding near the wire, widening outward), tube/line width ~0.035, color #1f7ac0. Each ring carries 1-2 arrowheads at roughly the bottom-front of the circle showing circulation: for I to the right (+X), circulation is counterclockwise when viewed from +X looking back toward -X (right-hand rule), which in this three-quarter view reads as arrows coming down the near side. Label 'B' with overbar vector arrow, bold black, placed above the rightmost ring set at (10, 3.2, 0). Radial marker: short line from wire axis at x = 7 outward in +Y (and slightly toward viewer) to radius r, with a highlighted amber #e8a33d ring of that radius drawn in the same plane; readout text near the marker. Physics: B = mu0*I/(2*pi*r) with I = 10 A, so B(microtesla) = 2.0/r(cm); at r = 1.5 cm B = 1.33 microtesla, at r = 6 cm B = 0.33 microtesla. Slider r in cm maps to world radius via world_r = 0.42 * r_cm so that r = 1.2 cm sits on the innermost ring and r = 6 cm on the outermost. Background white.
interactionPlan.notes: Build rings as THREE.TorusGeometry (thin tube) or Line loops in the Y-Z plane, grouped per set so the whole group can be rotated 180 degrees about Y, or arrowheads swapped, when current reverses. Arrowheads: small ConeGeometry oriented tangent to the ring; store tangent sign in a uniform/state so the toggle just negates it (animate the flip over ~400 ms so the reversal is visibly continuous). Hand can be a low-poly stylized mesh or a flat billboarded sprite/SVG texture facing the camera; if billboarded, mirror it horizontally on current reversal and re-point the thumb. Wire uses MeshStandardMaterial with low roughness plus a thin emissive highlight strip; render the wire after/through ring groups with correct depth so near rings occlude the wire and far rings are occluded (no depthWrite tricks needed if geometry is real 3D). Keep OrbitControls limited to azimuth -60..60 deg and elevation -20..45 deg so the figure never flips. Labels (I, B, readout) as CSS2DObject/HTML overlays anchored to world positions so they stay crisp and upright while orbiting.

discrepancies: The gripping fist is much less anatomically defined than the source: it reads as a cluster of skin-colored blobs with thin tubular fingers rather than a clearly closed fist with visible knuckles and nails, and the wire visually passes through the finger mass rather than being gripped by it.

Extra amber 'sampled field loop' with spoke and an inline 'r = 1.5 cm  B = 133 µT' readout sits in the middle of the third ring set; nothing like this exists in the source and it clutters that ring group.

Ring arrowhead density is lower than the source: the source shows an arrowhead on essentially every nested circle (mostly at the lower-near side pointing down), while the generated figure gives arrowheads only at one or two angles per ring, weakening the circulation read.

Relative scale is off compared with the source: in the source the fist is the dominant object, roughly as tall as the largest field circles and set close to the first ring set; here the hand is slightly small and set far left with a large empty gap before the rings.

The rings are slightly more foreshortened / perspective-convergent than the source's essentially flat side-on orthographic presentation, so the right-most ring sets look smaller than the left-most, whereas the source shows four equal-size sets.
evaluation.notes: Composition, colors and physics are right — horizontal wire, four sets of concentric blue field circles with tangential arrowheads, red current arrow with I, and a B vector label — with genuinely useful interactions (current reversal with arrow flip, 1/r radius slider, 4-step guided tour); main weaknesses are a crude, undersized fist, sparse ring arrowheads, and the added amber marker/readout that clutters one ring set.
action_items: Enlarge and refine the hand: make the fist roughly the height of the largest field circle, place it closer to the first ring set, and shape the curled fingers/knuckles and nails so the grip around the wire is unambiguous.
Add arrowheads to every nested ring (as in the source, biased to the lower/near side pointing downward for current to the right) so circulation direction is obvious at a glance.

Move the amber sampled-loop marker and its r/B readout off the ring set (e.g. to a dedicated cross-section plane at the right end or above the wire) so the default view matches the source's clean four-set layout.
Reduce perspective convergence (smaller FOV or orthographic default) so all four ring sets read as equal-sized, matching the source's side-on presentation.
plan_action_items: Specify a near-orthographic side view as the default projection since the source shows no ring-size falloff along the wire.
